Good morning. Here is your daily brief for Tuesday 2 June 2026.

Walthamstow: 16°C, light drizzle, high 19° / low 15°, 100% chance of rain.

GBP/USD 1.347 · GBP/ILS 3.824.

🚀 Israeli tech
- Kaltura, the Israeli video platform company, acquired eSelf, an AI avatar startup founded by a creator of Snap's AI systems, in a deal valued at 27 million dollars to integrate generative AI into enterprise video and learning tools. <https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/10/kaltura-acquires-eself-founded-by-creator-of-snaps-ai-in-27m-deal/>
- Israeli eVTOL startup AIR raised 23 million dollars in funding to scale production of both piloted and uncrewed cargo aircraft and expand into the United States market. <https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/30/air-secures-23m-to-boost-u-s-expansion-and-evtol-innovation/>
- Aporia, an Israeli AI safety company, had its Guardrails tool selected as one of TIME's 200 Best Inventions for 2024, recognized for mitigating evolving AI risks. <https://nocamels.com/2024/10/israeli-ai-safety-tool-among-times-best-inventions-for-2024/>
- So what for you: As a GTM advisor working with Israeli tech expanding into the UK, these acquisition and funding stories show the consolidation and deep-tech focus driving valuations—worth tracking which Israeli founders and teams are building AI products your clients might partner with or compete against.

🇬🇧 UK politics
- Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has warned of a "dangerous undercurrent" after the murder of Henry Nowak, with a police officer receiving death threats and being forced to relocate following footage of the victim being handcuffed while dying <https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/jun/02/shabana-mahmood-warns-of-dangerous-undercurrent-after-murder-of-henry-nowak>
- Two senior Labour policy figures, Mathew Lawrence and Mark McVitie, who previously backed competing visions for the party's direction, have joined forces to warn against tribalism within the party <https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/jun/02/labour-mathew-lawrence-mark-mcvitie-competing-manifestos-join-forces>
- Government ministers are facing criticism from both unions and employers over detailed plans to ban zero-hours contracts, proposing workers be guaranteed between eight and 20 hours per week based on regular hours <https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/jun/02/zero-hours-contracts-ban-firms-unions>
- So what for you: Starmer's focus on housing policy and the internal Labour debate about benefits funding could affect your mortgage options and ISA savings strategies as the government shapes economic direction over the coming months.

📱 Tech news
- Intel is experiencing supply shortages of its Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake laptop processors built on its new 18A process node, though the company downplays the issue as "some" shortages <https://www.techmeme.com/260602/p24#a260602p24>
- The UK has begun using SpaceX's militarized Starshield satellite network, making it among the first countries outside the US to adopt the technology <https://www.techmeme.com/260602/p23#a260602p23>
- SK Hynix Chair Chey Tae-won announced plans to double the company's memory chip capacity over five years in response to a global shortage that could persist until 2030 <https://www.techmeme.com/260602/p12#a260602p12>
- So what for you: Memory and processor shortages through 2030 will reshape enterprise infrastructure decisions you advise on, particularly for UK SaaS clients planning cloud and data centre commitments.

📰 Hacker News top 3
- Please don't spam people looking for employment. It's just cruel <https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48370330>
- Fidonet: Technology, Use, Tools, and History (1993) <https://www.fidonet.org/inet92_Randy_Bush.txt>
- Martin Scorsese Is Embracing A.I <https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/02/business/media/martin-scorsese-artificial-intelligence.html>

Today's question: Given that memory chip shortages could run until 2030, are your Israeli SaaS clients you're advising on go-to-market strategy already factoring longer infrastructure lead times into their UK expansion plans, or is that still being treated as an IT problem rather than a sales and delivery risk?
